items.title: Trump instructs Pentagon to reduce military exercises with South Korea
items.summary: UNITED STATES: US President Donald Trump has instructed the Pentagon to substantially reduce joint military exercises with South Korea, he said on Sunday in a social media post that also mentioned Seoul's refusal to take part in actions against Iran. The annual Ulchi Freedom Shield joint military exercises are scheduled to run from Aug 17 to 27, with about 18,000 South Korean military personnel participating. Trump wrote.

items.title: Rate shock, ringgit swings drive Tabung Haji's RM278mil London loss [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tabung Haji said its London property unit's RM278.4 million loss in 2023 was largely due to higher interest rates in the United Kingdom, weaker property valuations and currency movements. The loss at its investment vehicle LTH Property Holdings 3 Ltd (LTHP3), which bought Great Minster House for RM1.32 billion (£247.5 million) in 2022, comprised RM303 million in valuation losses and RM275 million in currency losses. £180 MILLION TO £202 MILLION ESTIMATE Universiti Teknologi Malaysia associate professor in property economics Dr Muhammad Najib Razali estimated that Great Minster House's value could have fallen to between £180 million and £202 million, based on estimated rental income and prevailing market yields.

items.title: Bus accident kills at least eight in Brazil
items.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO: A bus overturned in a steep, mountainous region north of Rio de Janeiro on Sunday, killing at least eight people, firefighters said in a statement. The Rio de Janeiro fire department said the accident had taken place early on Sunday near Petropolis, a mountain city north of Rio de Janeiro. Deadly road accidents are frequent in Brazil.

items.title: Tabung Haji weighs UK property exits as portfolio review begins [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tabung Haji is reviewing its exposure to property investments in the United Kingdom, including Great Minster House, as it maps out strategies to improve performance and address valuation gaps. The acquisition was reportedly Tabung Haji's sixth UK property investment, according to its former group managing director, Datuk Seri Amrin Awaluddin. The Great Minster House acquisition added to a UK property portfolio that Tabung Haji had been building since 2012.

items.title: Haze returns: What Malaysians need to know as air quality deteriorates
items.summary: Residents in several states, including Selangor, Negri Sembilan and Sarawak, are grappling with deteriorating air quality. As of Thursday (Aug 13) morning, air quality in 11 areas across the country was at unhealthy levels, with Sarawak the worst-affected state. Meteorologists have warned that without significant rainfall, the haze may persist, affecting air quality and public health across Malaysia.

items.title: Explained: Can a person be charged in a Malaysian hospital instead of a courtroom?
items.summary: Can an accused person be charged in a hospital ward? “Yes, the ward can be declared as open court and the proceedings can take place as if one was in the actual court concerned,” he said. Besides hospital wards, Sivananthan said a person could also be charged at other locations outside court.

items.title: Farmer’s coconut dehusking invention gets a shot at cracking the durian market
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 17 — An innovative coconut dehusking device developed by plantation entrepreneur Che Adnan Che Kadir, 56, which received a four-star rating, could now be adapted for durians and commercialised to meet the needs of the agricultural industry. Che Adnan said the judging panel at the Kelantan Department of Agriculture’s 2026 Agricultural Technology Innovation Competition proposed the idea after seeing the device’s potential for adaptation to other fruits. Che Adnan said he hoped that, once adapted for durians, the device could become a practical and safe home-grown innovation, while helping farmers and potentially reaching wider markets.

items.title: Trump says US scaling back military drills with South Korea
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Sunday he was "not happy" about US participation in joint military exercises with close ally South Korea and is scaling back the drills aimed at deterring rival North Korea that start Monday. "Based on my very good relationship with Kim Jong Un, of North Korea, I am not happy with the fact that the United States has, long ago, agreed to participate in Joint Military Exercises with South Korea," Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. Last Monday, Colonel Ryan Donald, spokesman for the US and South Korean Combined Forces Command, said the exercise would simulate combat against North Korean troops battle-hardened by deployment in the Russia-Ukraine war.

items.title: Trump welcomes defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Sunday he was pleased by the recent signing of a defence pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan. "Very happy to see that Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan have recently, and finally, signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement," he wrote on his Truth Social platform. The three-way agreement, signed Aug 7, comes amid a US-Iran war that has extended violence to the region, including Iran-backed Houthi rebel attacks.

items.title: K.O.I strikes gold with 'Tiwikarma'
items.summary: FIRST-TIME finalist K.O.I made history at the 40th Anugerah Juara Lagu (AJL 40), turning an electrifying, theatrical performance of 'Tiwikarma' into a winning moment on Saturday night. The hip-hop group captivated the judges with a dramatic performance at Unifi Arena, Bukit Jalil, overcoming strong contenders including Dayang Nurfaizah's 'Lemah' and Aina Abdul's 'Kamu' to take home the coveted grand trophy and RM100,000 cash prize. The trophies were presented by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, accompanied by Media Prima Bhd group chairman Datuk Seri Dr Syed Hussian Aljunid, Media Prima group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali and Media Prima Television Networks and Primeworks Studios chief executive officer Nini Yusof.

items.title: Malaysia braces for stronger El Nino, severe haze
items.summary: Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the southwest monsoon intensified the phenomenon, bringing hotter, drier conditions and raising the risk of fires across the region. Kurup said preparations for El Niño and the southwest monsoon began with the National Haze and Dry Weather Committee's first meeting of the year on June 15. He said measures would be carried out under the National Haze Action Plan and National Open Burning Action Plan, adding that Malaysia had stepped up regional coordination.

items.title: Aussie state to start gun buyback on Nov 2
items.summary: AUSTRALIA'S New South Wales state will start a gun buyback in November, said Prime Minister Anthony Albanese yesterday, as part of the national response to a shooting spree that killed 15 at a Jewish festival here. Albanese's centre-left government enacted laws in January for the gun buyback, tighter checks for gun licences and a crackdown on hate in the wake of the Dec 14 attack at a Bondi Beach Hanukkah celebration in Australia's most populous city. Australia had a record 4.1 million firearms last year, the government has said, with more than 1.1 million of those in New South Wales, its most populous state.

items.title: SD Property tops out first Elmina high-rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sime Darby Property Bhd (SD Property) has topped out Kanopi Residences, its first high-rise development in the 141.6ha Elmina City Centre in Sungai Buloh, Selangor. Located on Persiaran Garcinia near Elmina Lakeside Mall, Kanopi Residences is part of the City of Elmina masterplan and targets young professionals, first-time buyers and young families. SD Property chief operating officer of township development Appollo Leong said the topping-out milestone reflected the company's commitment to delivering quality developments on schedule.

items.title: Trump's 2024 grocery photo op now haunts Republicans in the midterms
items.summary: TWO years after Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump staged a New Jersey press conference flanked by grocery staples to spotlight inflation under Democrats, food prices are still rising despite his pledge to bring them down. Standing between tables piled high with fruit, beef, cereal, milk and other household staples at his Bedminster golf club on Aug 15, 2024, Trump blamed the Biden administration for sharp increases in groceries. The spectacle, complete with charts showing higher prices, was aimed at undercutting the Democratic nominee, Kamala Harris, and highlighted Trump's central promise: he alone could tame inflation and lower the cost of living.

items.title: Rafizi: Bersama is not Trojan horse for BN, Pas to defeat PH
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) is not a Trojan horse serving the interests of Barisan Nasional and Pas, Bersama co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said. "BN and Pas do not need an agent to defeat PH," he said during a Bersama gathering here last night. Rafizi said the "Trojan horse" narrative reflected how established political parties viewed Bersama's emergence rather than the party's actual purpose.

items.title: PKR has changed approach, now wants dissenters back, says Rafizi
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli said PKR's recent congress reflected a change in the party's political approach. Rafizi said PKR leaders previously appeared quick to tell dissenting members to leave, but its recent congress saw calls for former members to return. Rafizi also took aim at Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil's admission at the congress that PKR had a communication problem with the public.

items.title: DAP unlikely to quit govt before GE16, says Rafizi
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) co-founder Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli claimed DAP was unlikely to leave the government after having tasted power. Rafizi said DAP's extensive representation in government, from ministers and deputy ministers to state executive councillors, elected representatives and local councillors, made it difficult for the party to walk away despite disagreements within Pakatan Harapan. Rafizi said claims that DAP's special congress could result in the collapse of the Pakatan Harapan-led government were therefore misplaced.

items.title: Four prized Renaissance works stolen from museum in Sicily
items.summary: ROME: Four works "of extraordinary value" by Renaissance artist Antonello da Messina have been stolen from a museum in Sicily, Italy's culture ministry said Sunday. The theft, that includes three panels of the 15th century San Gregorio Polyptych, occurred late Saturday at a museum in Messina, the religious painter's hometown. The theft comes just months after the Italian state bought a work called "Ecce Homo" by Antonello da Messina at a New York auction in New York for nearly US$15 million (13 million euros).

items.title: PKR congress ends, but reformasi fight goes on, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2026 PKR National Congress has renewed the party's resolve to advance its reform agenda and strengthen its machinery to ensure its struggle continues to benefit the people, said PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's address served as a clear reminder that the "reformasi" struggle must continue and that the party's strength must always be anchored in the interests of the people. "Political challenges will continue to come, but Keadilan must remain steadfast in its principles and the people's struggle agenda," he said in a Facebook post.

items.title: Flores quake survivors cling to hope amid destruction
items.summary: MELANIA Nius was at her husband's hospital bedside on Indonesia's Flores island when a powerful quake shook their town to its core, sending patients fleeing into the chaos outside. Forty-eight people were killed in the quake, and dozens injured. "I just prayed: 'God, if you still give us the chance to live, please open a way for us'," she said.

items.title: Saudi Arabia issues alert for Jazan province along Yemen border
items.summary: RIYADH: The Saudi civil defence agency issued an alert on Sunday warning of "potential danger" in southern Jazan province along the border with Yemen that has been targeted by Yemeni rebels recently. "A warning has been issued by the National Early Warning Platform in the Jazan Province to alert of a potential danger," read the statement by the agency, with similar alerts usually issued ahead of potential strikes targeting an area. The Teheran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have repeatedly targeted energy and petroleum installations in Jazan in recent weeks.

items.title: 23 students to undergo eye misalignment surgery at HPUSM
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Twenty-three students aged between seven and 19 will undergo surgery for strabismus, or eye misalignment, at Universiti Sains Malaysia Specialist Hospital (HPUSM) over five days, helping to reduce a waiting period that could previously stretch from several months to years. HPUSM director Datuk Dr Ab Rahman Izani Ghani @ Ab Ghani said the surgeries were being carried out in conjunction with the second Strabismus Surgery Carnival, which runs from today until Aug 20. "Through the screening, HPUSM identified about 300 students with eye problems, including strabismus, and 23 of them will undergo surgery during the five-day carnival.

items.title: Hamas expects meeting with Kushner as US pushes Gaza plan
items.summary: CAIRO: Hamas sources said on Sunday that they expected to meet in Egypt with US envoy Jared Kushner, as President Donald Trump's administration seeks to push forward a Gaza peace plan rejected by Israel. "Mediators informed Hamas that US envoy Jared Kushner will hold a meeting with the Hamas leadership, in the presence of Egyptian and Qatari officials, before Kushner travels to Israel to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu," a Hamas source told AFP, requesting anonymity to discuss sensitive diplomacy. A second Hamas source said that the United States had sought clarifications from Hamas on several points including on "genuine, rather than merely symbolic, collection, consolidation and storage of weapons, as well as Hamas's complete relinquishment of governance of Gaza."

items.title: Gold shines as confidence in reserve assets fades
items.summary: GOLD is on the rise again, as a confluence of economic and political dynamics spurs demand from investors around the world, especially one cohort: central banks. After stalling around US$4,000 an ounce for several weeks, bullion has jumped around US$400, or 10 per cent, since the start of this month and could be on track for its best month this century. Investors weren't impressed by his remarks last month about the central bank's two per cent inflation goal.

items.title: Two dead, hundreds evacuated from fires on island near Athens
items.summary: ATHENS: Two people died and hundreds were evacuated Sunday after two fires broke out on the Greek island of Salamis near Athens, the fire department said. "It is a difficult fire... inside an inhabited area," he said. The fire department also had two vessels assisting, Artopios said.

items.title: NST Leader: Auku's abolition must usher in better regulation
items.summary: THE abolition of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Auku) is a welcome and significant reform, but its real test will be what fills the vacuum. Autonomy cannot mean universities simply inherit Auku's powers through internal regulations. Academic freedom must come with academic responsibility.

items.title: Woman who died after headscarf became entangled in water gate roller laid to rest
items.summary: SUNGAI BESAR: Department of Irrigation and Drainage worker Selaton Nuri, who died after her headscarf became entangled in the roller of a water gate yesterday, was buried tonight. The remains were then taken to her home in Kampung Bagan Terap about 5.30pm for her family to pay their last respects before being brought to Al-Mujahiddin Mosque in Pekan Bagan Terap for funeral prayers. After the prayers, the remains were taken to the Kampung Bagan Terap Muslim Cemetery and buried about 9.40pm.

items.title: Iran offers US$30,000 bounty for killing, capturing US soldiers
items.summary: TEHERAN: Iran's military announced on Sunday that it was offering a bounty equivalent to US$30,000 for killing or capturing US soldiers, with the reward doubled if carried out by a woman. There has been no known deployment of US ground forces in Iran during the Middle East war, with the exception of a rescue mission in April for a downed American airman. "Anyone who kills or captures and hands over an invading American military personnel will receive a reward equivalent to US$30,000 or 5 billion tomans from the Islamic Republic of Iran's Army," Hatami said, using an informal unit equivalent to 10,000 Iranian rials.

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Sunday, August 16, 2026

items.title: 15-year-old student dies after motorcycle crashes into trailer
items.summary: PENDANG: A secondary school student died after the motorcycle he was riding was involved in an accident with another motorcycle and a trailer along Jalan By Pass here today. District police chief Superintendent Rodzi Abu Hassan said police received a report on the accident about 1.40pm. "The accident was caused by the trailer being parked on the left road shoulder without the necessary warning signals," he said.

items.title: Government to amend Tabung Haji Act 1995, says Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government will amend the Tabung Haji Act 1995 to ensure that the trust of Muslims continues to be safeguarded, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the amendment was among the Madani Government's measures to strengthen governance and ensure that institutional weaknesses were addressed firmly. "Governance must continue to be strengthened, institutions cleaned up and every weakness firmly addressed.

items.title: Kelantan royal crown goes on public display for first time
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A centuries-old symbol of Kelantan's royalty is stepping into the public spotlight for the first time, with the Kelantan royal crown going on display at the Heritage Weapons Festival here. Kelantan Sultan's Office protocol officer Mohamed Safaruddin Ismail said the crown was one of the state's most significant royal artefacts and a symbol of the sovereignty of the Kelantan Sultanate. He said Sultan of Kelantan Sultan Muhammad V had consented to the crown being displayed publicly, giving visitors a rare opportunity to see it up close.

items.title: Farmers bring bananas, cassava and coconuts to settle 3 billion rupiah fine
items.summary: BENGKULU (Indonesia): Unable to pay a 3 billion rupiah (about RM688,000) fine, three farmers brought agricultural produce such as bananas, cassava and coconuts to court as payment after they were accused of cultivating land belonging to a palm oil company, reports said. In a report published by Kompas.com, the three farmers were Harapandi, 50, Rasuli, 53, and Ibnu Amin, 44. He said when they were asked to pay the fine, they could only bring agricultural produce they owned, namely cassava, bananas and coconuts, to the court.

items.title: Mat Sabu launches book, warns Malaysians against propaganda, urges facts over allegations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Accepting allegations without proper scrutiny could fuel ‘asabiyyah’, a tendency to defend one’s own group even when it is at fault while viewing the good deeds of others negatively, said Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. He said the public should not accept information blindly, but instead verify the facts and gain a clearer understanding before taking a stand. Mohamad said facts and knowledge were often harder to accept and took longer to digest, unlike accusations and suspicions that could spread easily, especially through social media.

items.title: Malaysian pilot detained in Jakarta, accused of smuggling RM45m drugs abroad since 2024
items.summary: Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations found that the 39-year-old man is believed to have used his flight schedule to transport drugs to several destinations. “This was not the first time, because he had transported drugs to several countries on several occasions,” he said when contacted. Hussein said the interrogation also led to the discovery of the existence of several drug trafficking syndicate networks operating in Malaysia and abroad, including Indonesia.

items.title: Minister calls nine‑year abandoned Tambunan Hospital project ‘sick’, pledges RM988,000 for urgent upgrades
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 16 — The new Outpatient Department (OPD) building project at Tambunan Hospital, which has been abandoned for nine years, will be resumed to improve the comfort of patients and staff. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the situation at the hospital was among the most disheartening things he witnessed during his working visit there today, with patients and staff having to cope with limited space. Dzulkefly also announced an immediate allocation of RM988,000 to address urgent needs at the hospital, with a large portion channelled towards upgrading the Emergency Department.

items.title: USM climbs 149 places in Academic Ranking of World Universities, now Malaysia’s top university
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 16 — Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) has risen to become Malaysia’s top-ranked university in the Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) 2026, climbing 149 places to rank 581st globally. USM said the achievement was significant as ARWU, also known as ShanghaiRanking, evaluates universities based on academic and research performance rather than reputation or perception alone. In ARWU 2026, USM recorded strong performance in the Publication (PUB) indicator, ranking 424th globally, while its HiCi indicator improved to 503rd worldwide.

items.title: Minister warns against immoral behaviour, stresses mosques and surau must remain sacred spaces
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Aug 16 — Muslims have been urged to observe proper conduct and good morals and refrain from immoral behaviour, especially in places of worship such as mosques and surau. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs), Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan, said mosques and surau are sacred places that must be respected and whose sanctity must be preserved. “I urge everyone to observe proper conduct, uphold good morals and comply with the law,” he told reporters after officiating at the closing ceremony of the Syariah Lawyers’ Sports Programme (SUKPES) at Universiti Tun Hussein Onn Malaysia (UTHM) here today.

items.title: Kelantan Health Department to monitor baby girl’s growth after testing positive for drugs
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 16 — The Kelantan Health Department (JKNK) will continue to monitor the development of a baby girl who tested positive for drugs after birth to identify effects on her mental development, growth and physical development. JKNK deputy health director (Medical) Dr Rohana Daud said continuous monitoring is important to ensure any effects on the baby can be identified, and appropriate action can be taken at an early stage. “Based on the information obtained, the baby’s mother had taken tranquilisers, and its effects on the baby are unlikely to be prolonged.

items.title: Widow of corporal electrocuted in Sabah to receive Sarawak rental aid, housing support
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 16 — The widow of Corporal Chiu Teck Siong, who died in an electric shock incident in Sabah on August 6, will receive aid under the Sarawak Rental Assistance Scheme (SRAS), said Sarawak Deputy Minister for Public Health, Housing and Local Government Datuk Michael Tiang Ming Tee. The Pelawan assemblyman said he would assist Tang Wei Wei, 39, in securing an affordable home, in addition to providing rental assistance under the scheme. Meanwhile, he said the government would bear the pre-school education expenses, including textbooks, for Tang’s youngest child, who is four years old.

items.title: MACC arrests two policemen over RM14,000 traffic offence bribes on East Coast Expressway
items.summary: “Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect is believed to have conspired to commit the act with another patrol police officer between January and July 2026. Meanwhile, the male patrol police officer in his 30s who was previously arrested on August 11 has had his remand extended by four days until August 19. The remand extension order was issued by the same Magistrate today after the first remand application for the police officer expired today.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution warns poverty and drugs, not racial fears, are Malays’ real enemies
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — The position of Malays in the country is not threatened by the existence of other races, but by poverty and social problems such as drug addiction, said Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) vice-president Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. The Home Minister said the real threat to the Malays is when they continue to be plagued by poverty and serious drug addiction. Malays are not under threat because there are Chinese in this country.

items.title: Three towns choke on unhealthy API, Serian tops list as haze blankets Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Three areas, including two in Sarawak, recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today. In Selangor, Johan Setia also recorded an unhealthy API reading of 124. Meanwhile, 65 other locations recorded moderate air quality levels.

items.title: Sarawak Education Department says Serian schools reopen tomorrow
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 16 — All primary and secondary schools under the Serian District Education Office (PPD) will operate as usual from tomorrow, the Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said in a statement today. “JPNS will continue to emphasise the welfare, health and safety of students, especially when facing hot weather or any unexpected weather conditions. 1 of 2019; Measures by the MOE to Ensure the Health and Safety of Students in Schools Located in Areas with Critical Haze Conditions dated Jan 15, 2019,” the statement said.

items.title: Saifuddin: End identity politics, focus on performance and economic recovery
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — PKR has called for an end to identity and racial politics, instead urging a greater focus on performance-based politics and economic recovery for the well-being of the people. “Malay identity, Islamic identity, Chinese identity, Indian identity, Sabah identity and Sarawak identity are all part of the reality of Malaysia. There is nothing wrong with identity.

items.title: Defend Malaysia’s ports, but identify firms abusing transshipment, says maritime expert
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — Malaysia should firmly defend its reputation as a trusted trading and shipping hub while conducting thorough checks to identify companies that may be abusing its ports to circumvent United States tariffs, said maritime industry observer Datuk Seri Jeyenderan Ramasamy. He said Malaysia should neither dismiss the concerns raised by the US nor allow broad allegations to cast doubt on the country’s entire maritime and logistics sector, stressing that authorities should demand evidence and investigate specific companies and cargoes. Identify the companies and cargo involved.

items.title: Status quo for now, DAP delegates vote to stay in govt
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP delegates today overwhelmingly voted for the party to remain in the federal government until the end of the current parliamentary term. Congress speaker Cha Kee Chin announced that 1,857 delegates voted to stay, while 242 voted to leave the government. Loke said DAP would respect the 12 per cent of delegates who voted to leave the government, but the party must follow the decision of the 88 per cent majority.

items.title: Anwar announces additional RM1m for every parliamentary constituency
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — The government has approved an additional RM1 million allocation for every parliamentary constituency nationwide, to be channelled directly towards addressing urgent needs and providing immediate assistance to the people. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the additional allocation would enable local needs, particularly those involving welfare, basic amenities and community issues, to be addressed more quickly without being hampered by excessive bureaucracy. He said the allocation demonstrated the Madani Government’s commitment to strengthening assistance for the people at the grassroots level.

items.title: PM Anwar vows full repeal of AUKU, no replacement laws curbing student freedom or movement
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — The government has given an assurance that the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) will be fully repealed without introducing any new laws that restrict or suppress student movements. “I also do not agree with any amendment or replacement (law) that restricts or suppresses student activities,” said Anwar, who is also PKR president. “Students are ordinary citizens.

items.title: Dungun doctor duped in forex, Ethereum scam, loses RM558,000 through 77 transactions
items.summary: DUNGUN, Aug 16 — A female doctor at a private clinic here lost RM558,000 after falling victim to an online forex and Ethereum coin investment scam since January. Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the 32-year-old victim initially saw an advertisement offering trading and investment lessons before contacting an individual via Instagram. District police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said the 60-year-old victim responded to a Facebook advertisement in June offering loans with low interest rates and attractive terms.

items.title: Diesel subsidy shake‑up coming soon; govt promises simpler rules, family quota transfers, easier access
items.summary: TAWAU, Aug 16 — Several improvements to the implementation of the targeted diesel subsidy system are being studied, with the government expected to announce them within the next one to two months, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Amir Hamzah said preparations for the 2027 Budget would ensure more effective and comprehensive delivery of assistance to the people under the targeted diesel subsidy. “Through the 2027 Budget Tour series, we are examining various improvements to the targeted diesel subsidy mechanism to ensure that those who are truly eligible can benefit from it optimally,” he said.

items.title: Nurul Izzah: I remain committed to same reform spirit since 1998
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 16 — PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar remains committed to the same spirit of struggle that drove the reform movement when it began in 1998, Sinar Harian reported today. According to the report, Nurul Izzah said although she would carry out her responsibilities through a different avenue in the future, her goals remained the same — strengthening institutions, preserving dignity and creating more opportunities for Malaysians. “PKR will continue to carry this responsibility.

items.title: PKR leaders vow fairness for all races, slam racial propaganda, urge unity over ego
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — PKR must continue to defend a fair political approach to all sections of society, while respecting the position of Islam and the Malays in the Federal Constitution. PKR vice president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the position of Islam and the Malays is a core element in the Federal Constitution that must be respected by all parties. In line with Amirudin, PKR vice president Datuk Seri R. Ramanan wanted PKR to remain firm in defending the diversity of races in this country and strongly reject actions that use racial issues as political capital.

items.title: Anwar says any decision on Umno must prioritise people’s welfare, ‘not anger’
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told party delegates today that he chose to put the people first, amid growing internal censure against the party’s unity government ally Barisan Nasional. Speaking at this year’s congress, Anwar said any decision regarding PKR’s cooperation with BN and Umno must not be driven by anger, but instead treated carefully through what he described as political “wisdom” that ultimately puts national interests above partisan conflicts. “It must always be driven by public and national interests.

items.title: Woman punched, threatened in OUG parking row; KL police arrest three suspects with records (VIDEO)
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 16 — Police have arrested three men after a woman reported being assaulted and threatened during an alleged illegal parking fee collection near the OUG community hall in Jalan Awan Besar. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said three suspects, aged between 20 and 26, were detained following the incident. Police urged the public to report any information on crime to the Brickfields police hotline at 03 22979222, the Kuala Lumpur hotline at 03 21159999, or the nearest police station.

items.title: Malaysian Qualifications Agency says abolition of AUKU cannot be taken lightly, urges clear guidelines
items.summary: Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA) chief executive officer Prof Datuk Dr Mohammad Shatar Sabran said any changes to the higher education legal framework must be made comprehensively and carefully to avoid gaps in terms of regulations, governance and institutional monitoring. He said the higher education system needs clear guidelines and procedures to ensure that university management and administration remain orderly and accountable. “Any decision regarding the abolition of AUKU must be preceded by a comprehensive approach as recommended by the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT), including a comprehensive assessment of the implications of changes to the higher education ecosystem.

items.title: Sarawak skies turn grey, DOE warns haze plumes from Kalimantan push API into danger zone
items.summary: Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said two other areas, Samarahan and Kuching, recorded API readings of 155 and 132, respectively, believed to be due to haze smoke moving in from various directions. She said 65 other areas recorded moderate air quality levels. Azuri Azizah said moderate smoke plumes were observed over southern and western Kalimantan, while light, localised smoke plumes were detected in southern and central Sumatra.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution made PKR’s de facto number two as Nurul Izzah steps down
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 16 — Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution will take over the duties of PKR’s deputy president after incumbent Nurul Izzah Anwar announced she would “take leave”. Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the handover at the party’s congress here this afternoon, where Nurul Izzah also gave a parting speech that called on the party to unite and galvanise its “differences” as a form of strength. Anwar also gave full authority to PKR vice president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari to direct the party’s election campaigns, a move he suggested would streamline preparations and strategies to avoid confusion in the chain of command.

items.title: At DAP congress, most delegates back staying in Anwar govt, urge faster reforms
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — DAP delegates debating whether the party should remain in the federal government today have largely backed staying until the end of the current term, while urging Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to accelerate reforms promised to Malaysians. Speaking during the party’s national congress here, several delegates argued that leaving the unity government now would amount to abandoning voters and handing political advantage to rival parties. Perak delegate and Sitiawan assemblyman Jason Ng Thien Yeong said his position was simple: DAP should remain in the government until the end of the term.

items.title: At DAP congress, Sangeet urges rethink of ties with Anwar, says PM has divided coalition, empowered Umno
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 16 — Wanita DAP legal bureau chief Sangeet Kaur Deo today called on the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) to reassess its relationship with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, ahead of a vote at the national congress on whether DAP should remain in the federal government. While favouring DAP’s continued participation in the federal government, Sangeet said the current coalition arrangement under Anwar had failed to unite its partners. She said the party could not ignore growing racial divisions and corruption-related scandals during its time in the federal government, warning that its silence on these issues had affected public confidence.
